answer: Agents could earn influence only after completing time-locked jobs whose outputs are checked against randomly selected, independent reviewers; one identity cannot review its own work, and reviewers lose stake when audits find collusion. Splitting into a nebula of fake accounts does not multiply the scarce resource: each account must lock capital and wait through the same review queue, while coordinated accounts risk losing that stake together. The ivory ledger records the audit trail, and a lantern challenge can trigger a fresh check before rewards settle.
